title: tenant-segmented-pin-rollout-validation-with-traffic-safety-guards
creator: Ana Patel
description: We need a robust pattern for rolling new pinned model revisions that: 1) isolates by tenant (org/account) and user cohorts, 2) runs orthogonal A/B metrics alongside functional canaries, and 3) enforces cost/latency SLO gates with automated rollback. Current pin swap behaviors are global and neglect tenant-level variability (cold KV caches, long-tail latency). This ticket defines the product-level rollout flow, telemetry gates, and UX controls for customers to perform tenant-segmented canaries and A/B tests behind a pin. Deliverables: product spec, console UX mock, acceptance criteria, rollout playbook, and handoff to ENG for orchestration implementation.
acceptance_criteria: Console: 'Pin Rollouts' page supports defining tenant cohorts (by org ID, region, or tag) and assigning weights per cohort.
Runtime: traffic split applied per-cohort such that different tenants can receive different revision weights simultaneously.
Telemetry: per-cohort dashboards show latency P50/P95, token cost delta, safety signal rate, and QA eval pass rate for synthetic prompt sets.

Gating: automated rollback triggers on any cohort when either latency delta > 30% above baseline (P95) OR token-cost-per-response increases by > 20% for sustained 10 minutes, or safety/regression alerts exceed configured thresholds.
A/B: support parallel A/B experiments within a cohort where hypothesis metrics (quality/accuracy) are tracked and can be tied to rollout decisions.
Playbook: documented staged-ramp policy with non-linear weight increases (0.5% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100%) and minimum observation windows between phases.
Privacy: rollout must respect tenant-level data isolation; logs and synthetic eval sets are tenant-tagged and access-controlled via RBAC.
Observability: ability to run a simulated preview (mirror traffic) and a synthetic prompt run before any live traffic ramp.
Operational: handoff artifacts (API spec, runbook, and GH PR links) created for ENG and SRE with clear rollback commands.
Documentation: user-facing docs and a security FAQ published in the Console docs before GA.
steps: Write product spec describing tenant segmentation model and how it maps to existing pin objects (pin -> revision -> per-cohort weight).
Define telemetry requirements: telemetry keys, sample rates, synthetic prompt set per-vertical, and dashboards/alerts with thresholds.
Design Console UX for selecting tenants/cohorts, configuring ramp schedule, and specifying A/B hypotheses/metrics.
Prototype a staged-ramp playbook with hysteresis to avoid flapping during short spikes.
Coordinate with ENG to expose APIs for per-cohort weight assignment and to ensure Dedicated autoscaler interactions are safe.
Create synthetic prompt suites (privacy-preserving) for top 5 customer verticals and wire into the eval harness.
Define rollback automation: what constitutes automatic rollback vs. manual operator action and how notifications are sent.
Author runbook for SRE and on-call including commands, dashboards, and escalation paths.
Ship initial feature flag behind enterprise customers for beta testing and collect feedback.
Iterate on thresholds and ramp timings based on beta telemetry and finalize for GA.
notes: Rationale: tenants have different traffic distributions and cold-cache effects; a global canary misses localized regressions and cost anomalies.
Trade-offs: increasing per-cohort granularity increases orchestration complexity and state; aim for a pragmatic first-cut with 'tag-based cohorts' instead of freeform tenant lists.
Fallback: define compatible fallbacks (e.g., quantized variant or previous revision) to route when resources constrained.
Cost: surface estimated token-cost delta per cohort in the Console before committing a ramp to help customers make informed choices.
Privacy note: synthetic prompt sets must be scrubbed and stored with per-tenant access controls; consider short TTL for raw traces.
Open question: whether per-cohort KPIs should be factored into global routing decisions (e.g., temporarily deprioritize tenants causing regressions).
